2609.19124.title: Flag Game: A Toy Model for Mechanistic Swarm Interpretability
2609.19124.paper_summary: Emergent coordinated behaviors of AI agents are starting to present critical safety risks. A key phenomenon driving these behaviors is the rapid formation and spread of beliefs about the world, and mechanistic understanding is crucial for collective alignment. To this end, we introduce the Flag Game, a toy model for studying the mechanisms of collective belief formation. Concretely, a hidden country flag defines the ground truth, and each bounded agent directly observes only a private crop but can exchange beliefs and weigh social evidence from peers. Despite its simplicity, the Flag Game reproduces rich collective phenomenology: non-monotonic scaling of performance with population size, accuracy gains from social-awareness prompting and team diversity, and strong effects of organizational structure. In particular, we identify that collective belief collapse at small population sizes turns into collective belief polarization as the population grows. This polarization causes the performance decline at large population sizes, but creates diversity in collective beliefs. Finally, we dissect the mechanisms underlying collective belief collapse and polarization with two complementary approaches. We first introduce social circuit attribution, a technique to predict which agent, and what view, matters most to collective dynamics, and verify its predictions by causal interventions on agents, tracing how agent patching changes collective outcomes. However, the efficacy of causal interventions on agents decreases as the population grows. We therefore develop a statistical mechanical theory for larger populations and verify that it matches the empirical phase diagram. Together, these results take a first step toward mechanistic swarm interpretability, a science of how the properties of individual agents and their communication give rise to emergent collective behavior.
2609.19124.paper_summary_zh: AI代理的緊急協調行為開始顯示出關鍵的安全風險。驅動這些行為的一個關鍵現象是對世界信念的快速形成和擴散，而機械理解對於集體對齊至關重要。為此，我們引入了旗幟遊戲，一個用於研究集體信念形成機制的玩具模型。具體而言，一面隱藏的國旗定義了真實情況，每個有界代理僅直接觀察到一個私有的作物，但可以交換信念並權衡來自同儕的社會證據。儘管其簡單性，旗幟遊戲再現了豐富的集體現象學：隨著人口規模的變化，表現的非單調縮放，來自社會意識提示和團隊多樣性的準確性提升，以及組織結構的強大影響。特別是，我們發現，在小規模人口中，集體信念崩潰隨著人口增長轉變為集體信念極化。這種極化導致在大規模人口中表現下降，但在集體信念中創造了多樣性。最後，我們通過兩種互補的方法剖析了集體信念崩潰和極化的機制。我們首先引入社會電路歸因，這是一種預測哪個代理及其觀點對集體動態最重要的技術，並通過對代理的因果干預來驗證其預測，追踪代理修補如何改變集體結果。然而，隨著人口增長，對代理的因果干預的有效性降低。因此，我們為更大的人口發展了一個統計力學理論，並驗證其與實證相位圖相匹配。總的來說，這些結果邁出了機械性群體可解釋性的第一步，這是一門研究個體代理的特性及其通信如何產生緊急集體行為的科學。
